summary.text: Brad Finstad is the Republican incumbent in Minnesota's 1st District. A fourth-generation farmer from the New Ulm area, he worked in congressional staff, agricultural-association and USDA roles and served three terms in the Minnesota House before winning a 2022 special election to Congress. His campaign website lists his issue positions.

paragraphs.text: Brad Finstad was born in New Ulm, Minnesota, in 1976, and his official biography describes him as a fourth-generation farmer and resident of the New Ulm area.
He graduated from the University of Minnesota with a degree in agriculture education and an emphasis in Rural Leadership Development.
He worked as a staffer for U.S. Rep. Mark Kennedy (R) and as executive director of the Minnesota Turkey Growers Association and of the Center for Rural Policy & Development.
Finstad served three terms in the Minnesota Legislature, representing House District 21B beginning in 2003, and later served as state director for USDA Rural Development in Minnesota.

He was elected to Congress in a special election on August 9, 2022, and was sworn in three days later; he won full terms in November 2022 and November 2024 and won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary.
His office lists his committee assignments as House Agriculture (where he chairs the Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture Subcommittee), Armed Services, and Small Business.
According to his official biography, Finstad and his wife Jackie have seven children and operate an agriculture business in New Ulm with extended family on a generational family farm.
